title: Require context-aware pre-release testing and staged rollout for generative content features
description: Illustrative reference decision modelled on the Google Gemini image-generation controversy. Not a documented decision of any specific organization.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty.

Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources). Normalized a duplicated relationship-reason phrasing ("...via this design pattern." -> "...via this single, primary design pattern.") to one canonical wording.

decision_statement: Before broadly releasing a generative content feature, the organization must test its output against a diverse, context-specific set of prompts — including prompts where a safety or fairness adjustment could plausibly conflict with factual/historical accuracy — and release to a limited audience first, with a fast feedback and rollback path, before full public availability.
decision_context: Motivated by Google Gemini's image generator producing historically inaccurate depictions after a fairness-tuning adjustment was applied without testing its effect on factual/historical prompts specifically.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Generative Content Safety Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Apply a single global safety/fairness adjustment across all prompt types without context-specific testing.
Release directly to full public availability without a staged rollout.

citations.title: Gemini image generation got it wrong. We'll do better.

relationships.reason: This decision is modelled as a direct governance response to this incident.
The decision is put into practice via this single, primary design pattern.
Context-specific pre-release testing directly satisfies this control's intended-context requirement.
Compliance must be demonstrated by a documented content safety review report.
Boards adopting this decision should be asking whether pre-release testing covers context-specific failure modes.
